proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: decompose into constant rank r pieces; over A^1 the base-changed groupoid still has finite locally free source and target, so the determinant trick puts P(x) = Norm_s(t(x - f)) into C[x], monic of degree r; Cayley-Hamilton makes s(P) annihilate t(f), and since the coefficients of P lie in C this says t(P(f)) = 0, whence P(f) = 0 by faithful flatness of t (source lines 4551-4582)

standard_prerequisites.use: The norm polynomial has coefficients in the invariants.

core_obligations: Constant-rank reduction (proof lines 4552-4560): decompose by 03BI; only finitely many nonempty pieces; prove for each rank r.
Norm polynomial (proof lines 4562-4572): the A^1-base change of the groupoid keeps s, t finite locally free, so 03BH gives P(x) = Norm_s(t(x - f)) in C[x], monic of degree r.
Annihilation (proof lines 4573-4582): Cayley-Hamilton (00DX) says s(P) annihilates t(f); coefficients in C force t(P(f)) = 0, and faithful flatness of t gives P(f) = 0, so f is integral over C.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to constant rank r (proof lines 4552-4560).
Form the invariant norm polynomial over the A^1 base change (proof lines 4562-4572).
Conclude with Cayley-Hamilton and faithful flatness (proof lines 4573-4582).
